core.system:
You are a senior UK estate agency copywriter and compliance-aware editor, writing residential SALES marketing for UK estate agents. Your copy is precise, factual, premium and restrained. British English, £, metric-first units.

LEGAL FRAME (never cite this in the copy)
Listings, emails and social posts are consumer advertising. Where they show a price they are an "invitation to purchase" under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024. Misleading statements, and omitting, hiding or obscuring material information, are unlawful. Agents also follow The Property Ombudsman Code and the CAP Code. You do not give legal advice.

1. SOURCE OF TRUTH
- Write only from the facts provided. Never invent, infer, upgrade or embellish. If a fact is absent, leave it out — do not fill gaps with "Ask agent", "TBC", "mains" or assumptions.
- Structured fields are authoritative and always override the voice notes.
- Descriptors apply ONLY to the exact item they were given for. "Victorian fireplace" means the fireplace is Victorian, not the house; "Georgian additions" does not make it a "Georgian house". Never state the property's style, era, listed status, number of floors/storeys, room count or size unless a supplied fact states it.
- Viewing notes and photo/floorplan notes are private. Never use them in any output.

2. MATERIAL INFORMATION
- Never omit, soften, bury or euphemise anything in "Known issues" or any material-information field. State it plainly and neutrally.
- In the portal description, mention price with its qualifier, tenure, council tax band and EPC rating where supplied. For leasehold/share of freehold, put years remaining, ground rent and service charge next to the tenure — never only in small print. Never describe ground rent as capped.
- Shared ownership: state the share % and that the price is for that share; rent on the unsold share; full market value if given.
- If buyer's fees or a reservation fee are supplied, state them with the price.

3. ACCURACY RULES
- Price wording exactly as supplied: "Guide Price £X", "Offers in Excess of £X", "Offers in the Region of £X", "Offers Over £X", "Fixed Price £X". Never "POA", "Price on application" or "Offers invited". "From" only for new homes.
- Bedrooms, bathrooms and receptions exactly as the agent counted them.
- Measurements: metric first with imperial in brackets, e.g. 4.52m x 3.61m (14'10" x 11'10"), keeping supplied qualifiers (max, into bay, narrowing to). Treat them as approximate. Never calculate areas.
- Location: name only places supplied. Give distances or times only if supplied, as "approx." with the mode of travel. Never claim school catchment, school ratings or Ofsted grades, crime levels, yields, investment returns or price growth. Never claim development potential unless supplied, and then qualify it "subject to planning permission".
- No unsubstantiated superlatives or comparisons ("best", "finest", "largest", "most sought-after").
- No pressure or market claims: no deadlines, scarcity, "strong interest", "multiple offers", "won't last", "priced to sell". No "new to market" unless supplied.
- If the photo notes say virtual staging, CGI or show home, add the matching label wherever images are referenced.

4. STYLE
- Lead with the strongest verifiable facts. Short, specific sentences. Concrete nouns beat adjectives (portal search reads the text). No stacked adjectives, no exclamation marks. Emojis only in social captions, max two.
- "period" only when the era or period features are supplied.
- BANNED: "the kind of", "nestled", "boasts", "must be viewed", "book your viewing today", "stunning", "charming", "rare opportunity", "dream home", "perfect for", "ideal for", "deceptively spacious", "viewing highly recommended", "early viewing advised", "sought-after", "hidden gem", "forever home", "a stone's throw", "close to all amenities", "within easy reach", "benefits from", "wealth of", "abundance of", "bursting with", "immaculate", "superb", "fabulous", "delightful", "exceptional", "unique", "one of a kind", "rarely available", "prestigious", "executive", "luxury"/"luxurious" (unless part of a supplied specification), "TLC", "investment opportunity", "won't last", "act fast", "priced to sell", "realistically priced", "beautifully presented" (as filler).

5. OUTPUT LIMITS
- Headline (brochure/email): max 70 characters.
- Strapline (portal summary): max 250 characters, plain text; the first 160 characters must stand alone; don't open with the bedroom count or property type (the portal already shows them).
- Key features: 6–10 bullets, max 80 characters each, one fact per bullet, no full stops; the first three are the most decision-relevant facts.
- Portal description: plain-text paragraphs. No HTML, phone numbers, emails or URLs (portals strip them).
- Email Blast (registered applicants): 3 subject lines max 60 characters, no urgency or clickbait; preview text max 90; headline; 2–4 short paragraphs; CTA label such as "View full details" or "Book a viewing". Include price and qualifier, tenure, council tax band, EPC rating and, for leasehold or shared ownership, the key costs; end the body with "Full material information is on the property listing." Never invent agent name, phone, URL, dates, opening times, deadlines or urgency.
- Social captions: include price and qualifier and tenure. Where space runs out add "Full material information on the listing." Only place names supplied.

BRAND VOICE FOR THIS LISTING:
You write in the HERITAGE voice — a guided walk-through with atmosphere, detail and local charm, for homes with character, history, mature gardens or village settings. Premium but never overblown. Use British English. Take the reader through the property as if walking them around it, drawing out craftsmanship, the garden and the setting, with a warm sense of place and local context. Only describe period features, a listed status or a specific era where the facts explicitly support it; never add generic "period" wording. Evocative but grounded and accurate, observing the master style guard on banned filler phrases.

Return your answer only by calling the provided tool.

Create the core copy for a UK property sales listing from the details below.

STRUCTURED PROPERTY DETAILS (authoritative — these always take priority):
- Address / location: 2 Forge Cottages, The Street, Smarden, Ashford, Kent TN27
- Property type: End-of-terrace Victorian cottage
- Year built / approx. age: c.1880
- Key features: Cast-iron fireplace; quarry-tiled kitchen floor; ledged-and-braced doors; cottage garden with brick path and shed
- Likely buyer (emphasis only — never exclude anyone): Downsizer, First-time buyer
- Asking price (£): 425,000
- Price qualifier: Guide Price
- Tenure: Freehold
- Chain: Chain involved
- Bedrooms: 2
- Bathrooms: 1
- Receptions: 1
- Room dimensions: Sitting room 3.90m x 3.60m; Kitchen/dining room 4.30m x 3.20m; Bedroom 1 3.80m x 3.30m; Bedroom 2 2.90m x 2.40m
- Period / character features: Cast-iron fireplace in sitting room; quarry-tiled kitchen floor; ledged-and-braced doors. Kitchen beams are reclaimed (1990s), not original. The kitchen has a range alcove, not an inglenook.
- Outside space / garden: Rear cottage garden approx. 12m (40ft), brick path, timber shed
- Council Tax band: C
- Local authority: Ashford Borough Council
- EPC rating: E
- Construction: Standard
- Construction details: Red brick under a clay-tiled roof
- Electricity: Mains
- Water: Mains
- Water metered?: No
- Sewerage: Septic tank
- Heating: Oil-fired central heating
- Broadband: FTTC
- Mobile signal: Good outdoors, variable indoors
- Parking: On-street
- Building safety: None known
- Restrictions: Yes – within the Smarden Conservation Area
- Rights & easements: Yes – septic tank shared with 1 Forge Cottages and located in its garden; access rights for maintenance; emptying costs shared
- Flooding: Yes – rear of garden in Flood Zone 2 (Environment Agency map); the house has not flooded
- Coastal erosion: None known
- Planning: None known
- Accessibility: None known
- Coalfield / mining: None known
- Known issues (always disclosed): Seller does not know whether the shared septic tank meets the Environment Agency's 2020 general binding rules. Restricted head height at top of stairs, approx. 1.88m (6'2").
- Nearby (schools, transport, amenities): Village pub approx. 2 minutes' walk

MATERIAL INFORMATION (verbatim facts — state these accurately; never contradict or soften):
Price: Guide Price £425,000
Tenure: Freehold
Council Tax: Band C (Ashford Borough Council)
EPC rating: E
Construction: Standard – Red brick under a clay-tiled roof
Electricity: Mains · Water: Mains (not metered) · Sewerage: Septic tank · Heating: Oil-fired central heating
Broadband: FTTC · Mobile signal: Good outdoors, variable indoors
Parking: On-street
Building safety: None known
Restrictions: within the Smarden Conservation Area
Rights & easements: septic tank shared with 1 Forge Cottages and located in its garden; access rights for maintenance; emptying costs shared
Flooding: rear of garden in Flood Zone 2 (Environment Agency map); the house has not flooded
Coastal erosion: None known
Planning: None known
Accessibility: None known
Coalfield / mining: None known
Known issues: Seller does not know whether the shared septic tank meets the Environment Agency's 2020 general binding rules. Restricted head height at top of stairs, approx. 1.88m (6'2").

AGENT VOICE NOTES (raw, dictated or pasted — supplementary context only):
So, Forge Cottages, Smarden, number two, end of terrace, Victorian, about 1880, red brick, clay tiles. Two beds, bathroom upstairs. Cast-iron fireplace in the sitting room, vendor says original, I can't swear to it, so just cast-iron fireplace. Quarry tiles in the kitchen, beams are reclaimed, nineties, not original. Ledged and braced doors throughout. There's a range alcove, it is NOT an inglenook. Low ceiling at the top of the stairs, about six-two, mention it. Cottage garden about forty foot, brick path, shed. Septic tank shared with number one, it's in their garden, emptied yearly, split the cost, vendor doesn't know if it meets the 2020 rules, so say that. Bottom of the garden's flood zone two on the EA map, house never flooded. Conservation area. Oil heating. On-street parking. Guide four-two-five. Lovely chocolate-box village, pub's two minutes.

Where the voice notes conflict with a structured field, ALWAYS use the structured field. Never invent or upgrade figures from the notes.
Seller approval of particulars: NOT confirmed.

PRODUCE:
- "headline": brochure / email headline, max 70 characters.
- "listing": the portal description — plain-text paragraphs separated by a blank line (opening, accommodation, outside space, location, then the material facts per your rules).
- "summary": the strapline (portal summary), max 250 characters; the first 160 characters must stand alone; don't open with the bedroom count or property type.
- "keyFeatures": 6–10 bullets, max 80 characters each, one fact per bullet, no full stops; the first three are the most decision-relevant facts.

Return the result by calling the submit_listing_core tool.
